title: Fourth moment bound from Fourier irregularity
statement: Let $n$ be a natural number and let $f:\mathbb F_2^n\to\mathbb R$. Suppose $\epsilon\ge0$ and that there is a nonempty set of coordinates whose Fourier coefficient for the corresponding sign-cube representation of $f$ has absolute value greater than $\epsilon$. Then $\epsilon^4\le \sum_{\gamma\in\mathbb F_2^n}\widehat f(\gamma)^4-(\mathbb E f)^4$, where $\widehat f(\gamma)$ denotes the Fourier coefficient indexed by $\gamma$.
hypotheses_covered: function f from the binary cube to the reals
the sign-cube representation of f is not ε-Fourier-regular
caveat: The supplied definitions do not specify the Fourier coefficient conventions or the precise identification of the binary cube with the sign cube.
